about: The coverage each assembly reaches, held in both directions. A score under its entry is a suite that weakened; a score over its entry is an entry that has stopped describing the tree it sits in, and both are refused. Checked by .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js, which the coverage workflow runs. One entry per assembly, never one number for the repository: the host project's pages and controllers are covered through API tests, and a combined figure would let engine coverage fall while the total held steady.
howToRaise: A floor is measured, never chosen. Run the coverage command below and write the percentage the check prints for that assembly. Raise a floor in the same change that raises the coverage; a floor above the measured score reds the check immediately, which is the mistake this sentence exists to prevent, and since #188 a floor left under the measured score reds it too, so the sentence is now held rather than only written. Do not round the report's rate attribute down by hand. A rate is written to at most four decimal places and the attribute carries the float form of that value, so 0.9583 is stored as 0.9582999999999999, and rounding those digits down records a hundredth less than the suite reaches. That is where two of the four entries below sat until this file was corrected. The printed percentage is the same rate multiplied by a hundred and rounded to two decimals, which moves nothing while the report keeps to four, and the check compares the rate itself with a billionth of a point of slack for the float form, so a floor taken off the printed row compares equal rather than above. A collector that starts writing a fifth decimal would break that, and the repair then is to read the rate rather than the row.
command: dotnet test --configuration Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults && node .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js TestResults

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.measured: line-rate 0.9416 and branch-rate 1 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above run on Windows against the branch landing the administrator API, with 823 tests passing on each leg. BOTH FIGURES ROSE IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT RAISED THE COVERAGE. The API is a controller over the rule store and the vocabulary tables, and every arm of it is reached: each of the seven endpoints on its success path, a name that is not a bare file name on the read, the create, the update and the delete, a document the validator refuses on the create and on the update, a create over a name the store holds, a read, an update and a delete of a name the store does not hold, a body that is not JSON, and a store with no directory answering the vocabulary. The assembly reports 742 of 788 sequence points executed and 160 of 160 branch slots covered on the run these rates are read from. What it reported before this change is not restated here, because the entry that stood recorded rates for this assembly and no counts, and a count reconstructed from a rate is arithmetic rather than a measurement. BRANCH COVERAGE IS NOW WHOLE FOR THIS ASSEMBLY, which is a statement about the branches it declares and not about the lines: forty-six sequence points are still unexecuted and they are the two classes the notes below name, neither of which declares a branch. The store gained a delete, a name predicate and a refusal sentence, and the arm answering false for a name the directory does not hold is reached by a test rather than left to the API, which resolves a name against the listing before deleting and cannot reach it. Both target frameworks were measured and the two reports carry these same two rates. The machine has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg ran on the .NET 10 runtime under DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major, which means the two builds agreed rather than two runtimes. THE FIGURES THIS ENTRY CARRIED BEFORE were line-rate 0.9068 and branch-rate 0.96, taken against the branch declaring the id member with 240 tests passing on each leg. Both figures were raised from 90.12 and 95.83 in the same change that raised the coverage, which is what the note above asks for. What raised them is the scan refusing a document whose id another document already holds: the refusal is new executed lines and new covered branch slots in RuleDocumentLoader and nothing unexecuted arrives with it. Both target frameworks were measured and the two reports carry these same two rates. The machine has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg ran on the .NET 10 runtime under DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major, which means the two builds agreed rather than two runtimes.

Both moved UP again with #70, and again with the change coalescer in #35, and both of those ARE new tests rather than an accounting change. Two classes hold everything unexecuted in this assembly. Plugin.cs is at line-rate 0.0714 and needs a server to construct. LibraryManagerChangeSource is at line-rate 0: it is a constructor and six event accessors forwarding to the server's own library manager, and the only way to execute one is to hold a real ILibraryManager, which means a running server. What the suite covers instead is the type on the other side of that port, LibraryChangeSubscription, at line-rate 1 and branch-rate 1. PluginServiceRegistrator is at line-rate 1, RuleDocumentStore is at line-rate 1, and LibraryChangeCoalescer is at line-rate 1 and branch-rate 1. Both figures moved UP again with the rules directory scan in #26, which is new code at line-rate 1 and branch-rate 1 rather than a change to anything already counted here.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.branchNote: NO PARTIALLY COVERED BRANCH POINT IS LEFT IN THIS ASSEMBLY, which is what the branch figure of 1 says and is the one direction of this entry that cannot rise again. The six-clause name check that used to sit at condition-coverage 83.33% is now a predicate the store and the API both ask, and both of its answers are reached from both callers, which is what closed it. A branch added tomorrow that no test reaches reds this entry immediately rather than eroding a fraction. THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE described that six-clause check as the only partial point and read: Every partially covered branch point left in this assembly is in RuleDocumentStore, at branch-rate 0.875. Plugin.cs, PluginServiceRegistrator, RuleDocumentLoader, LibraryChangeSubscription, LibraryChangeCoalescer and LibraryManagerChangeSource all report branch-rate 1 over the branches they declare, the loader's own id-collision arm included: both directions of it are reached, by a directory holding two documents that claim one id and by one holding two that do not. The report puts what is unexecuted on one line, RuleDocumentStore.cs:128 at condition-coverage 83.33% (10/12), which is the six-clause name check that refuses a name composing into a path outside the store's directory. It short-circuits on the first clause that matches, so a name refused by an early clause never reaches the later ones and no set of inputs lights every slot. The coalescer's three defensive arms are inside that branch-rate 1 rather than outside it, and reaching them is why the suite's fake clock can move without running a timer and can run a timer that is not due: a timer is a request and not a promise, so a callback that arrives early, arrives late or arrives with nothing to do is an ordinary input rather than an impossible one.

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.branchNote: The only partially covered branch point in the assembly is still the discard in the value-kind description in RuleDocumentValidator, reported at condition-coverage 87.5% (7/8). The compiler requires it for exhaustiveness and no input reaches it, because a member that is absent is refused before anything describes its kind. Its line number is not recorded here any more: it moves whenever anything is added above it in that file, and it has moved twice for that reason without the arm itself changing. Read it off the report rather than from this note. The second describer beside it, added with the name member, has both arms reached and adds no partial point, and the id member's own refusals add none either: every arm of the set check, the length check and the two kind checks is reached by a test. The value types add no partial point either. Every arm of every reader is reached: each type has a test accepting its form and a test refusing the value the neighbouring type would accept, the duration walk is reached at each of its refusals including the years-and-months arm and the overflow, and both arms of the bound that cuts a quoted value are reached, by a value at the bound and by one whose cut would otherwise land inside a surrogate pair. The operator table adds no partial point either. Both arms of the acceptance walk are reached, by a pair the table accepts and by one it does not; both arms of the value-type refusal are reached, by an operator that takes a value and by one that takes none; and the two arms that throw rather than answer, an operator with no row and a refusal asked for a pair the table accepts, are each reached by a test. The composition stage adds no partial point either. Every refusal in the walk is reached by a document written to trip it, both directions of the group-count check are reached by an object carrying one member and by one carrying two, the depth arm is reached at the deepest allowed level and one past it, and the member walk is reached by a condition, by a nested group and by a member that is not an object. The field vocabulary adds no partial point either. Both arms of the row walk in the table are reached, by a field that has a row and by one that does not; both arms of the name lookup are reached, by a declared name and by a name differing from one only by case; and every arm of the stage that reads a condition's field is reached, by a condition naming a declared field, by one carrying no field member, by one whose field is not a string, by one naming a field the table does not declare and by a nested group holding each of those. The pointer resolver's arms are reached the same way: an empty pointer, a pointer with no leading slash, an absent member, an index past the end of an array, a token that is not a number, a descent into a value that is neither object nor array, and both escapes in the order the standard decodes them. The operator table's second type column adds no partial point either, and it is the one entry here where every arm is a copy of an arm already described: both directions of the field-type walk are reached, by an operator that applies to a field of the type asked about and by one that does not, and both arms of the field-type refusal are reached, by a pair the table refuses and by the accepted pair it throws for rather than answers. The stage that reads a condition's operator adds no partial point either. Every arm of it is reached by a document written to trip it: a condition with no operator member, one whose operator is a number rather than a string, one naming an operator no operator has, one naming an operator that does not apply to a field of that field's type, one naming an operator the field's own row does not declare, and one that is accepted. The two narrowed refusals beside it are reached the same way, including both arms of the guard that throws rather than building a refusal for a pair the field accepts. The stage that reads a condition's value adds no partial point either. Every arm of it is reached by a document written to trip it: a condition writing no value where the operator takes one, a condition writing no value where the operator takes a list, a value beside an operator that takes none, an operator that takes none and is written correctly, a list where one value belongs, one value where a list belongs, an empty list, a member of a list that does not parse beside members that do, and a value that does not parse where one belongs. The dispatch beside it is reached at each of its seven arms and at the throw a type with no reader takes, and the third column on the operator table is reached in both directions, by an operator written with a list and by one written with a value. The type a value is parsed against is reached on both of its answers, the field's own type and the operator's single one, and on both ways of asking for a pair that has no answer. The compile table and the stage that walks a rule's conditions onto a query add no partial point either. Both arms of the pair lookup are reached, by a pair the table compiles and by one over a field it compiles with an operator it does not; both arms of the property claim are reached, by a document narrowing two properties and by one narrowing a property another condition already wrote; both arms of every write that can decline are reached, by a value the property carries and by one it cannot, and the year check is reached at each of its two comparisons; and both arms of the guard on the write are reached, by a query and by a null one. The reporting arm in MembershipApplier adds no partial point either. Each of its three levels is asked whether it is enabled before the line is built, and both the level test and the outcome test above it are reached on both answers: a collection whose membership moved, one the run left exactly as it was, and one whose apply threw, each against a logger that reports every level enabled.
